title: Etiquette & language
body:
Three official languages share the country: Luxembourgish is the everyday spoken language, French dominates shops, menus and signage, and German shows up in print media. Around 80% of the population also speaks English, but opening with "Bonjour" rather than English is the local norm and is well received.

A brief handshake is the standard greeting, including in casual encounters with shopkeepers and waitstaff — cheek-kissing is reserved for people who already know each other. Luxembourgers tend toward reserved, polite phrasing over overt friendliness; it isn't coldness, just the register.

Punctuality is taken seriously for any timed booking or tour.
